All good men were stunned, until Saint-Andrassy, Bossuet’s Vicar, who as a witness and arbiter knew everything that had been done by the Bishop in this matter, exposed the most shameful frauds. Then indeed the indignation of all erupted; the work was reported to the sacred tribunals; antidotes against the plague were sought. Meanwhile, Quesnel, having been established as the head of the faction after Arnauld, and Gerberon, having scattered seditious pamphlets through Belgium and France, as was related above, having taken the opportunity especially from the aforementioned case of conscience, stirred up everything; and now the unbridled license of those men seemed to be curbed only by applied force. But this was the labor. Quesnel, having frequently changed his hideouts, clothes, and assumed names, being called now Father Prior, or Provincial of the Augustinians, now Monsieur de Frefne, Frekerberg, Baron de Rebeck, du Puis, etc., had hitherto eluded the industry of the most sagacious men.
